data.name: ScreensMapName
data.value: Map of the screens with the SensorPanel's position

data.name: PanelScreenDescription
data.value: The panel always belongs here. If this screen goes away, the panel waits for it to come back.

data.name: HostScreenDescription
data.value: Windows that open on the panel screen are moved here.

data.name: ScreenNumbersDescription
data.value: Shows each monitor's number from the map on that monitor.

data.name: StatusReturning
data.value: The SensorPanel is going back to its screen.

data.name: StatusElevation
data.value: AIDA64 runs as administrator, so Windows does not allow moving the panel. Run SensorPanelPin as administrator.

data.name: StatusElevationNotInstalled
data.value: AIDA64 runs as administrator, so Windows does not allow moving the panel. Install SensorPanelPin: it then starts with administrator rights at every logon.

data.name: StatusChooseScreen
data.value: Choose below which screen the SensorPanel belongs on.

data.name: StatusWaitingForScreenFormat
data.value: {0} The panel stays where it is until the screen comes back.

data.name: StatusNoPanel
data.value: No SensorPanel window in sight. Turn on the SensorPanel in AIDA64.

data.name: SaveFailed
data.value: Could not save the settings to disk. They apply until the program closes; details are in the log.

data.name: KeepPositionDescription
data.value: Restores the remembered position on the screen. When off, only the screen is kept: the panel stays on the right monitor.

data.name: RestoreSizeDescription
data.value: When the panel changes size, it goes back to the remembered one.

data.name: GeometryFormat
data.value: {0}, {1} px from the screen's top-left corner, size {2} × {3}

data.name: GeometryNotSet
data.value: Not remembered yet. It is learned when the panel first appears on its screen.

data.name: TopmostDescription
data.value: AIDA64 may remove this setting. Turning it on in the SensorPanel options of AIDA64 itself is more reliable.

data.name: HideFromAltTabDescription
data.value: The panel does not show up in Alt+Tab.

data.name: PanelRuleHeader
data.value: How to recognise the panel window

data.name: PanelRuleDescription
data.value: The defaults fit AIDA64. Change them only if the panel is not found.

data.name: RuleClassDescription
data.value: An asterisk stands for any run of characters, a question mark for one character.

data.name: RuleTitleDescription
data.value: An empty field matches any title.

data.name: CheckMatchDescription
data.value: Lists every AIDA64 window and marks the one that matches the fields above.

data.name: RelocateHeader
data.value: Move windows off the SensorPanel screen

data.name: RelocateDescription
data.value: Windows cannot stop programs from opening on a chosen screen. A window that appears there is moved to the screen for other windows.

data.name: ExceptionsDescription
data.value: These windows stay where they open.

data.name: ProblemsDescription
data.value: A window that still comes back to the panel screen after three bursts of moves is left alone until the end of the session.

data.name: NoProblems
data.value: No window has kept coming back to the panel screen.

data.name: AutoStartRegistryDetail
data.value: The panel is not managed if AIDA64 runs as administrator: Windows will not let it be moved.

data.name: AutoStartElevatedDetail
data.value: Through Task Scheduler, with no UAC prompt at each logon. Needs the program installed in Program Files.

data.name: StartPausedDescription
data.value: The program starts but leaves windows alone until you resume it.

data.name: VerboseLogDescription
data.value: Records every pass. Useful for tracking down problems; takes a few MB a day.

data.name: SafetyPollDescription
data.value: How often to check positions even when nothing happens.

data.name: DebounceDescription
data.value: So that dragging a window does not trigger a correction every moment.

data.name: DebounceName
data.value: Wait after a window moves, in milliseconds

data.name: DisplayDelayDescription
data.value: How long to give Windows to arrange the screens after plugging in, waking up or changing resolution.

data.name: DisplayDelayName
data.value: Wait after a screen change, in milliseconds

data.name: PingPongLimitDescription
data.value: After this many moves in a short time, a window gets a break.

data.name: PingPongLimitName
data.value: Number of moves in a burst

data.name: PingPongWindowDescription
data.value: The time in which the moves above are counted.

data.name: LocationWarningFormat
data.value: The program runs from a folder ordinary users can change, so it cannot start with administrator rights. Install puts it in C:\Program Files\SensorPanelPin, where only administrators can change it. {0}

data.value: Could not determine the path to {0}. Autostart was not changed, so that no wrong entry gets registered.

data.value: Could not write the autostart entry to the registry.

data.name: AutoStartNeedsElevation
data.value: This option needs administrator rights. Choose “Restart as administrator” from the tray icon's menu, then pick the option again.

data.value: Removing the task from Task Scheduler needs administrator rights. Choose “Restart as administrator” from the tray icon's menu, then pick the option again.

data.name: AutoStartTaskRemoveFailed
data.value: Could not remove the task from Task Scheduler.

data.name: TrustOwnerFormat
data.value: “{0}” belongs to {1}, not to the administrators.

data.name: ElevationNoExecutable
data.value: Could not determine the program's path.

data.value: Could not restart with administrator rights.

data.value: The target screen's coordinates cannot be trusted right now.

data.name: StatusBackoff

data.name: StatusNeedsElevation
data.value: AIDA64 runs as administrator. Run SensorPanelPin as administrator.

data.name: TrayLogDisabledFormat
data.value: Logging was turned off for safety: {0}

data.name: TrayElevationText
data.value: AIDA64 runs as administrator, so Windows does not allow moving its window. Choose “Restart as administrator” from the tray icon's menu.

data.name: DiagnosticsIntro
data.value: The window marked “MATCHES RULE” is treated as the SensorPanel. If none is marked, adjust the “How to recognise the panel window” fields.

data.name: AlreadyRunning
data.value: SensorPanelPin is already running. Its icon is in the notification area.

data.name: LegacyRunning
data.value:
An older version of this program (SensorPanelGlue) is still running. Two copies would fight over the same windows.
Quit it from its tray icon's menu, then start SensorPanelPin again.

data.name: FatalErrorFormat
InstallNeedsAdministrator
data.value: Installing and uninstalling need administrator rights. Start them from the SensorPanelPin settings, which ask for those rights.

data.name: InstallDoneFormat
data.value:
SensorPanelPin is installed in {0} and starts with Windows, with administrator rights. It is running now; its icon is in the notification area.
The downloaded folder is no longer needed.

data.name: InstallUntrustedFormat
data.value: The installed copy can be changed by ordinary users, so no task with administrator rights was created: {0}

data.name: UninstallDescription
data.value: Removes the program and its autostart entry and, if you choose, its settings and logs.

data.name: UninstallAskSettings
data.value:
Also remove your settings and logs?
Yes removes everything. No keeps the settings for a later installation.

data.name: UninstallDoneAfterRestart
data.value: SensorPanelPin is uninstalled. A few files that were in use are removed at the next restart.

data.name: OfferInstallInPlaceFormat
data.value: Another copy of SensorPanelPin is already running. Install this copy (version {0}) in its place?
